articles.title: Mendonça revoga prisão domiciliar de ex-'número 2' do INSS preso em operação contra fraudes | G1
articles.standfirst: Adroaldo Portal foi preso pela PF em dezembro do ano passado, e é investigado após planilha do 'Careca do INSS' citar pagamentos em espécie destinados a 'Adro'.
articles.summary: Adroaldo Portal foi preso pela PF em dezembro do ano passado, e é investigado após planilha do 'Careca do INSS' citar pagamentos em espécie destinados a 'Adro'.
articles.body:
O ministro André Mendonça , do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ), revogou a prisão domiciliar do ex-secretário-executivo do Ministério da Previdência Social Adroaldo Portal, investigado pelo esquema de fraudes em benefícios de aposentados e pensionistas do INSS.

Com a decisão, o ex-servidor terá de usar tornozeleira eletrônica e cumprir restrições impostas pela Justiça, como proibição de contatos com outros investigados e de deixar o país.

A PF investiga depósitos em espécie realizados na conta do investigado Adroaldo, que totalizaram R$ 249,9 mil, as demais movimentações financeiras apontadas suspeitas e o registro de R$ 50 mil destinado a “Adro” encontrado em planilha apreendida no contexto das diligências.

A planilha pertence ao empresário Antônio Camilo Antunes, chamado de "Careca do INSS" e apontado como principal operador do esquema.

Adroaldo Portal, secretário-executivo do Ministério da Previdência — Foto: Vinicius Loures/Câmara dos Deputados

🔎Em abril do ano passado, investigações da PF revelaram um esquema criminoso para realizar descontos irregulares de valores recebidos por aposentados e pensionistas do INSS, ocorridos no período de 2019 a 2024. Os desvios, conforme as investigações, podem chegar a R$ 6,3 bilhões.

Mendonça afirmou que os elementos que justificaram a prisão continuam em apuração, mas o cenário mudou diante do afastamento e exoneração do cargo.

Adroaldo Portal estava em prisão domiciliar porque é pessoa com deficiência física e demanda cuidados especiais e contínuos, não integralmente disponíveis no ambiente prisional.

“Nesse aspecto, assume particular relevância a alteração objetiva da situação funcional. Um dos fundamentos da decisão originária para considerar existente risco à instrução dizia respeito à elevada posição então ocupada por Adroaldo no Ministério da Previdência Social, da qual se extraiu a possibilidade de influência sobre servidores, documentos e sistemas administrativos. Ocorre que o investigado foi inicialmente afastado do cargo por decisão judicial e, posteriormente, exonerado. A fonte específica de poder institucional que serviu de fundamento à cautela foi, portanto, substancialmente neutralizada”, escreveu o ministro.

Segundo Mendonça, “não se identifica, nos documentos ora examinados, indicação de ato concreto de Adroaldo praticado após seu afastamento destinado a constranger servidores, alterar ou suprimir documentos, acessar indevidamente sistemas, combinar depoimentos ou, por qualquer outro mecanismo, perturbar a investigação”.

Para o relator, diante desse cenário a monitoração eletrônica é adequada.

"A defesa de Adroaldo da Cunha Portal recebe com serenidade a acertada decisão do Supremo Tribunal Federal, que acolhe os fundamentos jurídicos expostos e reconhece a desnecessidade da manutenção da segregação cautelar, em adequada aplicação dos princípios da proporcionalidade e da excepcionalidade das prisões processuais.

A defesa permanece convicta da inocência de seu constituinte e confiante no pleno esclarecimento dos fatos".

articles.title: De olho no Lula 4, Centrão garante vitória do ajuste fiscal, mas governo precisa dar segundo passo | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente da Câmara deixou claro que o governo precisa adotar novas medidas fiscais, e que o ideal seria enviá-las ainda este ano ao Congresso.
articles.summary: Presidente da Câmara deixou claro que o governo precisa adotar novas medidas fiscais, e que o ideal seria enviá-las ainda este ano ao Congresso.
articles.body:
De olho na montagem dos ministérios do próximo governo Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), os partidos do Centrão ajudaram o presidente a obter uma vitória nesta segunda-feira (23) na Câmara dos Deputados , em operação comanda pelo presidente da Casa, Hugo Motta (Republicanos-PB).

Com isso, o ajuste fiscal do governo foi aprovado na Câmara por um placar folgado, 353 votos a favor e 128 contra. As principais legendas do Centrão garantiram ao governo 178 votos. Os líderes destes partidos estão negociando com o presidente do PT, Edinho Silva, espaços no próximo governo.

Afinal, ontem o mercado começou tenso por causa do ajuste fiscal e do cenário internacional. O dólar chegou a bater em pouco mais de R$ 6, mas recuou ao longo do dia, fechando em R$ 5,93, valor do fechamento da última quinta-feira. Sexta-feira (20) foi feriado.

Discussão e votação de propostas legislativas — Foto: Vinicius Loures / Câmara dos Deputados

Os partidos do Centrão deram a maioria dos seus votos para a vitória do governo. Uma maior divisão foi observada só no PP. O governo conseguiu votos até no oposicionista PL, sete votaram a favor da proposta e Lula.

Do placar da vitória na votação do texto-base, 353 votos a favor e 128 contra, o Centrão ficou assim:

O MDB, que forma mais a frente ampla, também votou majoritariamente com o governo. Foram 33 sim e 4 não. O PSDB, que negocia uma federação com os emedebistas, deram 15 votos sim e um não.

No PT, 67 votaram sim e três não votaram: Lindbergh Farias e Natália Bonavides se abstiveram e Kiko Celeguim não registrou presença.

Agora, a dúvida é sobre quando virão as medidas da segunda etapa. Enquanto os investidores cobram, o ministro da Fazenda, Dario Durigan, com o aval do presidente Lula, já começa a fechar as medidas fiscais da segunda etapa que serão focadas em conter o crescimento das despesas obrigatórias.

A dúvida, porém, permanece. Durigan será o responsável pela implementação destas medidas e elas serão anunciadas ainda neste ano.

articles.title: Ajuste fiscal: PSOL não vota a favor e deputados do PT se abstêm | G1
articles.standfirst: Câmara dos Deputados aprovou na noite de segunda-feira (23) plano que prevê economia de até R$ 56 bilhões para governo Lula; proposta segue para sanção.
articles.summary: O ajuste fiscal do governo Lula foi aprovado na Câmara para economizar R$ 56 bilhões, apesar da resistência do PSOL e das abstenções de parlamentares do PT.
articles.body:
Deputada Erika Hilton (PSOL - SP) — Foto: Renato Araújo / Câmara dos Deputados

A bancada do PSOL na Câmara dos Deputados não entregou nenhum voto a favor do ajuste fiscal proposto pelo governo Lula ( PT ) na noite dessa segunda-feira (23). Os 13 parlamentares do PSOL optaram pela obstrução ou pela abstenção - não votaram nem sim nem não.

Ainda assim, o plano, que deve trazer uma economia de até R$ 56 bilhões em 2027, teve o texto-base aprovado na Câmara, por 353 votos a favor e 128 votos contra .

Além do PSOL, três deputados do PT deixaram de votar, sendo que dois deles registraram críticas ao projeto do governo e se abstiveram: Lindbergh Farias (RJ) e Natália Bonavides (RN). O PT tem 67 deputados e registrou 64 votos favoráveis ao ajuste, 2 abstenções e 1 ausência.

O posicionamento chama a atenção porque políticos do PSOL e do PT formam a base de apoio do governo Lula e foram importantes cabos-eleitorais do presidente na campanha pela reeleição neste ano.

No PSOL, dez deputados se posicionaram pela obstrução, uma ferramenta usada para tentar atrasar a votação de um projeto. Outros três se abstiveram de votar: Erika Hilton (SP), Professora Luciene Cavalcante (SP) e Célia Xakriabá (MG).

Erika Hilton, deputada reeleita com recorde de 1,5 milhão de votos, justificou a decisão em vídeo nas redes sociais. De acordo com Erika, a Faria Lima "tentou colocar uma faca no pescoço do governo Lula" para exigir cortes, mas o presidente teve "coragem" de "enfrentar os interesses dos poderosos".

"Mas existem pontos que nós discordamos, e por isso o meu voto foi pela abstenção. Um deles é a exclusão da receita extraordinária do petróleo do cálculo do piso da saúde. Outro, que me preocupa ainda mais, é a possibilidade de reduzir de 2,5 para 2 o limite de crescimento real das despesas públicas em determinadas circunstâncias", afirmou Erika Hilton.

"Embora isso não altere diretamente os pisos da saúde e da educação, pode acabar comprometendo a capacidade de investimento do Estado brasileiro nessas pautas."

A deputada Fernanda Melchionna (PSOL-RS) justificou a atitude do partido: "A bancada do PSOL, de forma unânime, não deu nenhum voto a favor do ajuste para nós. Isso é motivo de coerência partidária." Na tribuna do plenário da Câmara, Fernanda criticou a pressão do mercado financeiro sobre o governo Lula.

"É preciso pegar o calor do segundo turno para colocar uma nova agenda econômica para o Brasil, para o governo Lula dar certo e para o povo brasileiro garantir direitos", afirmou a deputada.

Discussão e votação de propostas legislativas. Dep. Fernanda Melchionna (PSOL - RS) — Foto: Vinicius Loures / Câmara dos Deputados

Os dois deputados do PT que optaram pela abstenção, Lindbergh e Natália Bonavides, fizeram questão de consignar o apoio a Lula, apesar das críticas ao projeto em votação.

"Me insurjo porque sou Lula", afirmou Lindbergh na tribuna, quase sem voz. "O que a gente tinha que aprovar aqui era mais força para Lula e menos para o mercado financeiro."

O deputado petista atribuiu aos juros altos o motivo de a economia não estar melhor. "O Brasil pede um debate sobre como fazer para impedir a recessão econômica. O mercado quer golpear Lula. Eu não vou votar favorável."

Discussão e votação de propostas legislativas. Dep. Lindbergh Farias (PT - RJ) — Foto: Vinicius Loures / Câmara dos Deputados

Natalia, como Erika Hilton, reconheceu pontos positivos da proposta de ajuste fiscal, como o enfrentamento aos supersalários e a redução de benefícios tributários, mas fez ponderações.

"Nossa preocupação é que o ajuste fiscal não comprometa a capacidade de investimento do Estado, nem restrinja recursos fundamentais para as políticas públicas e os direitos sociais", escreveu Natalia em nota publicada nas redes sociais.

"Somos Lula! Somos PT! Somos parte do projeto político liderado pelo presidente Lula."

Confira como outros partidos de esquerda, que compõem a base de Lula na Câmara, votaram nessa segunda-feira no projeto de ajuste fiscal:

articles.title: Deputado Marcelo Rangel (PSD) fecha acordo para não ser processado por usar funcionários da Alep em campanha eleitoral no Paraná | G1
articles.standfirst: Promotoria afirma que três assessores parlamentares dele, pagos com dinheiro público, tiveram função desviada na campanha de 2024, quando Rangel concorreu à prefeitura de Ponta Grossa.
articles.summary: Promotoria afirma que três assessores parlamentares dele, pagos com dinheiro público, tiveram função desviada na campanha de 2024, quando Rangel concorreu à prefeitura de Ponta Gro
articles.body:
O deputado estadual Marcelo Rangel (PSD) fechou um Acordo de Não Persecução Cível (ANPC) para não ser processado pela suspeita de usar funcionários da Assembleia Legislativa do Estado do Paraná (Alep) na campanha eleitoral de 2024, quando ele concorreu ao cargo de prefeito de Ponta Grossa , cidade dos Campos Gerais.

O acordo foi homologado pela Justiça neste mês de novembro e indica que o Grupo de Atuação Especial de Combate ao Crime Organizado (Gaeco) obteve indícios de que três assessores parlamentares de Rangel, pagos com dinheiro público, não prestaram serviços à Alep entre 16 de agosto e outubro de 2024 devido ao desvio de função.

O fato é considerado uma improbidade administrativa — que é, entre outros atos, usar o trabalho de servidores públicos em serviços particulares.

O g1 e a RPC , afiliada da TV Globo no Paraná, entraram em contato com a assessoria de imprensa e o escritório de advocacia que atua na defesa de Rangel, e também com o diretório paranaense do Partido Social Democrático (PSD), e aguardam resposta.

O acordo determina que, para não ser processado por improbidade administrativa, Marcelo Rangel deverá pagar R$ 75.439,75 .

Uma parte é ressarcimento do eventual prejuízo causado aos cofres públicos (quase R$ 50,3 mil) e deve ser direcionada à Alep, e outra é uma multa civil (de pouco mais de R$ 25,1 mil) cujo valor deve ir para o Fundo Estadual de Defesa dos Interesses Difusos.

O Acordo de Não Persecução Cível (ANPC) é um instrumento consensual previsto na Lei de Improbidade Administrativa (Lei nº 8.429/1992) que permite solucionar casos de improbidade sem a necessidade de condenação judicial.

Pela Constituição Federal, os atos de improbidade administrativa suspendem os direitos políticos de agentes e ex-agentes públicos pelo prazo de 5 a 8 anos, além de condenarem o servidor à indisponibilidade de bens e ressarcimento aos cofres públicos.

No entanto, a Lei Federal nº 14.230 alterou a Lei de Improbidade Administrativa em 2021 e tornou mais claras as regras para o chamado Acordo de Não Persecução Cível (ANPC).

Com isso, o Ministério Público tem autonomia para propor acordos que reduzem as penas dos condenados e devolvem o dinheiro gasto irregularmente aos cofres públicos mais rapidamente.

Marcelo Rangel (PSD) — Foto: RPC Ponta Grossa

Formado em Direito pela Universidade Estadual de Ponta Grossa (EPG), Marcelo Rangel Cruz de Oliveira tem 56 anos, é empresário, radialista e está no fim do terceiro mandato na Alep.

Ele foi eleito deputado estadual em 2006 e reeleito em 2010. Em 2012 foi eleito prefeito de Ponta Grossa, e reeleito em 2016.

Em 2020 assumiu a Superintendência Geral de Inovação do Paraná e em 2022 foi eleito para o terceiro mandato de deputado estadual (que encerra agora no fim de dezembro de 2026).

Em 2023, se licenciou da Alep para assumir a Secretaria de Estado da Inovação, Modernização e Transformação Digital (SEI) e retornou ao parlamento em maio de 2024.

Em outubro de 2024, concorreu novamente à Prefeitura de Ponta Grossa, mas ficou em terceiro lugar na votação. Em 2026, concorreu pela primeira vez ao cargo de deputado federal e não foi eleito.

articles.title: Entenda ajuste fiscal do governo Lula aprovado na Câmara dos Deputados | G1
articles.standfirst: Projeto define medidas que economizarão pelo menos R$ 56 bilhões em 2027, como cortes de incentivos e benefícios tributários, mudanças nas despesas discricionárias — que não têm pagamentos obrigatórios.
articles.summary: O ajuste fiscal de até R$ 56 bilhões aprovado pela Câmara prevê cortes em benefícios tributários, mudanças no piso da saúde e medidas para conter gastos públicos federais.
articles.body:
A Câmara dos Deputados aprovou nesta segunda-feira (23) o projeto de lei que realiza um ajuste fiscal nas contas públicas para que seja possível cumprir a meta do orçamento de 2027.

O Senado finalizou a votação na última quinta-feira (19) e o presidente da Câmara, Hugo Motta (Republicanos-PB), convocou sessão para segunda para analisar o texto, mesmo sendo um dia em que normalmente não há votação nos plenários do Congresso.

A votação acelerada foi um pedido do governo atendido por Motta diante do que ele chamou de "preocupação do Congresso com essa alta do dólar e a perspectiva de uma alta taxa de juros".

O ajuste fiscal foi enviado ao Congresso Nacional pelo governo. O projeto define uma série de medidas que podem levar a uma economia de até R$ 56 bilhões , pelas contas do senador Eduardo Braga (MDB-AM), relator no Senado, como cortes de incentivos e benefícios tributários, mudanças nas despesas discricionárias — aquelas em que não há imposição legal para serem realizadas.

Entenda as principais mudanças propostas pelo governo ( clique no menu abaixo para ir ao tópico ):

O projeto prevê mudanças nas regras de concessão de incentivos e benefícios tributários. A principal delas é a efetivação de uma defesa antiga do governo Lula (PT): o corte linear de 10% em benefícios que o governo dá a diferentes setores da economia.

O corte de benefícios é uma defesa do Ministério da Fazenda ainda sob o comando de Fernando Haddad (PT). No final de 2025, já houve o corte de 10%. Na época, o governo estimava um ganho de R$ 19,8 bilhões nas contas públicas.

Agora, o projeto encabeçado pelo ministro Bruno Moretti amplia esse corte em mais 10%. Ou seja, o corte linear nos últimos dois anos chegará a 20%.

Plenário da Câmara dos Deputados durante sessão conjunta do Congresso Nacional destinada à deliberação de Projetos de Lei — Foto: Carolina Curi/Agência Senado

Uma das mudanças mais criticadas pela oposição é a medida que autoriza o Executivo a limitar a utilização de créditos tributários para compensar outros impostos devidos à Receita Federal.

Atualmente, empresas que possuem créditos tributários podem deixar de pagar certos impostos.

🔎 Crédito presumido é um benefício fiscal que permite à empresa aproveitar valores pagos a mais anteriormente ao governo para pagar novos impostos devidos. Esse valor é calculado como imposto pago e reduz a carga tributária final da empresa.

Pelo projeto, o governo poderá estabelecer restrições a essas compensações, com percentuais diferenciados conforme o valor ou o tipo de crédito utilizado. A ideia é proibir a compensação cruzada, ou seja, usar crédito de um tipo de imposto para pagar outro tipo.

A medida poderá ser adotada em momentos nos quais o governo entre em contenção de gastos.

➡️ Na prática, a restrição pode aumentar a arrecadação em dinheiro no curto prazo, porque parte dos tributos que seriam pagos com créditos terá de ser efetivamente paga, em dinheiro, pelas empresas.

O trecho levou a duras críticas do setor produtivo. Em nota, 57 entidades criticaram o fato de o texto não determinar um prazo para as compensações retornarem depois de uma eventual decisão do governo.

"O texto não diz se o crédito retido será devolvido, em que prazo ou com que correção, e a regra valeria a partir da publicação da lei", diz a nota.

Outra medida que levou à crítica é a parte do projeto que altera a base de cálculo para determinadas despesas vinculadas à arrecadação, como o piso da saúde.

O texto prevê que, até 2030 , a receita do imposto sobre a exportação de petróleo não seja considerada no cálculo de determinadas despesas obrigatórias, como acontece hoje.

Segundo o ministro Bruno Moretti, a intenção é retirar receitas extraordinárias relacionadas ao petróleo da base de cálculo de despesas constitucionais. A exclusão dessas receitas reduz o montante que obrigatoriamente precisa ser destinado à área.

Moretti defendeu que a mudança segue a lógica de que a arrecadação com petróleo só cresceu de forma extraordinária devido ao aumento no preço do combustível causado pelo conflito no Oriente Médio e não é uma receita contínua, o que infla os gastos com o piso da saúde.

A ideia é não contar com ganhos extraordinários — que podem não acontecer no futuro – para a conta de gastos contínuos e que devem sempre ser realizados. Cálculos indicam que a Saúde pode deixar de receber cerca de R$ 9 bilhões em 2027.

A retirada dessas receitas do cálculo do piso já está em vigor em 2026, mas em caráter temporário. Com o projeto, a medida poderá ser prorrogada até 2030.

Um dos principais pontos do projeto é a alteração das regras de crescimento das despesas públicas. Atualmente, o arcabouço fiscal permite que os gastos federais cresçam, acima da inflação, entre 0,6% e 2,5% ao ano, dependendo do comportamento das receitas.

Com o projeto, quando o governo precisar cortar gastos para cumprir a meta, o teto será de 2%.

O texto também amplia a possibilidade de corte de despesas, permitindo que o Executivo bloqueie recursos mesmo quando a projeção do resultado das contas públicas estiver dentro da margem inferior de tolerância da meta fiscal.

Ampliação do rol de gastos que podem ser contingenciados

Atualmente, somente as despesas discricionárias, aquelas que o governo pode decidir se e quanto vai gastar, podem ser congeladas temporariamente (contingenciadas, no jargão econômico) para cumprir as metas fiscais.

Com a proposta, os gastos obrigatórios que não estão na Constituição Federal também estarão sujeitos à contenção. Segundo o economista Felipe Salto, esse conjunto de despesas representou R$ 388 bilhões em 2026.

Neste caso e no do gatilho adicional para a contenção de gastos, as mudanças são permanentes e valerão para todos os anos.

Uma medida para dar flexibilidade para o governo gerenciar o orçamento muda as regras sobre recursos com destinos específicos, como os fundos públicos. Com o projeto, até 40% do dinheiro que não for utilizado dos fundos no ano anterior poderá ser destinado a despesas públicas previstas na Constituição.

Para isso, o projeto altera a Lei de Responsabilidade Fiscal – que proíbe o uso dos saldos desses fundos. No entanto, o projeto atual mantém a proibição de remanejar recursos de áreas essenciais, como saúde, educação, segurança pública, seguridade social, desenvolvimento social e de repasses a estados e municípios.

O projeto também prevê medidas relacionadas aos chamados supersalários do funcionalismo público. O texto estabelece um prazo de até 60 dias para que o Congresso aprove uma proposta que regulamente os pagamentos de servidores acima do teto – atualmente cerca de R$ 46,3 mil.

O projeto não elimina diretamente os chamados penduricalhos , pagamentos adicionais que podem fazer a remuneração de servidores ultrapassar o teto. Isso terá que ser definido no Congresso Nacional.

O projeto altera os repasses anuais da União a estados e municípios para compensar perdas com a não cobrança do imposto estadual em exportações. O repasse, previsto na Lei Kandir, é atualmente de R$ 4 bilhões.

Com o texto aprovado pelo Congresso, a transferência será de R$ 2 bilhões por ano até 2030.

Apesar das medidas de contenção de despesas, o projeto também prevê uma flexibilização das regras fiscais para permitir gastos com subsídios ao diesel, que estão sendo feitos pela guerra no Oriente Médio.

A proposta autoriza o governo a desconsiderar até R$ 10,5 bilhões em despesas extraordinárias para estabilizar os preços do combustível na meta fiscal de 2026. Os recursos estão relacionados à concessão de subvenções econômicas a produtores e importadores de diesel.

A exclusão das despesas da meta fiscal não significa que os gastos deixarão de existir ou de afetar as contas públicas. A medida apenas permite que sejam desconsiderados na avaliação do cumprimento da meta fiscal.

articles.title: Vaga no STF: Lula cogita Simone Tebet e ministras do STJ e STM | G1
articles.summary: Para assegurar aprovação no Senado, o presidente Lula avalia indicar Simone Tebet ou ministras de tribunais superiores para ocupar a próxima vaga aberta no STF.
articles.body:
Depois do jantar com a cúpula do Congresso e ministros do Supremo Tribunal Federal , quando ficou convencido de que não há nenhuma possibilidade de reenviar o nome de Jorge Messias , o presidente Lula decidiu construir um nome alternativo para o STF .

Nesta linha, passou a cogitar a indicação de uma mulher para ter segurança de aprovação. Uma candidata teria menos chances de ser rejeitada no Senado .

Entre os nomes de mulheres cotadas para o cargo, três atualmente são ministras:

Maria Elizabeth Guimarães Teixeira Rocha , presidente do Superior Tribunal Militar (STM);

Regina Helena Costa , ministra do Superior Tribunal de Justiça (STJ);

Daniela Teixeira , ministra do Superior Tribunal de Justiça.

Outro nome cotado é o de Simone Tebet , ex-senadora e ex-ministra do Planejamento e Orçamento.

Lula sinalizou aos ministros do STF e a Davi Alcolumbre ter entendido que não tem condições de reenviar Jorge Messias .

Em contrapartida, também não enviaria o nome do ministro do Tribunal de Contas da União Rodrigo Pacheco .

Ou seja, nem o nome preferido de Lula, nem o de Alcolumbre. A dúvida é como o presidente do Senado pode reagir à posição do presidente depois de ter garantido seguidas vitórias para Lula.

Lula não quer indicar Rodrigo Pacheco depois da derrota que sofreu em abril, com a rejeição de Jorge Messias. Não descarta, porém, indicá-lo em próximas vagas.

Em 2028, Luiz Fux se aposenta. Em 2029 é a vez de Cármen Lúcia . Em 2030, mas, no final do mandato de Lula, em dezembro, Gilmar Mendes . Com isso, esta vaga acabará ficando com o presidente a ser eleito em 2030. A não ser que Gilmar Mendes se aposente antes para tentar fazer um sucessor.

O presidente brasileiro Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) em imagem de arquivo — Foto: REUTERS/Diego Herculano

articles.title: Ajuste fiscal de Lula: Bruno Moretti articulou aprovação na Câmara | G1
articles.standfirst: Câmara dos Deputados aprovou na segunda-feira (23) o do projeto de lei que realiza um ajuste fiscal nas contas públicas para que seja possível cumprir a meta do orçamento de 2027.
articles.summary: O ajuste fiscal de Lula, articulado por Bruno Moretti, projeta impacto de R$ 56 bilhões até 2027 e enfrentou votos contrários de nomes como Lindbergh Farias e Erika Hilton.
articles.body:
O ministro do Planejamento e Orçamento, Bruno Moretti, foi o principal formulador e também o principal negociador do governo para aprovar o projeto de ajuste fiscal do governo do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), aprovado na Câmara dos Deputados, na segunda-feira (23) .

O ministro também atuou para tentar reduzir as resistências ao texto, principalmente entre parlamentares de esquerda do PT, PSOL e PCdoB.

Na segunda-feira (23), Moretti também esteve com Lula no Palácio da Alvorada, residência oficial da Presidência da República, nas últimas conversas antes da votação do projeto.

Também estiveram no Alvorada o ministro da Fazenda, Dario Durigan, e o senador Eduardo Braga (MDB-AM), relator do projeto no Senado Federal .

Antes da análise do tema pelo plenário da Câmara, Moretti se reuniu com as bancadas do PSOL e do PCdoB. Durante a discussão da proposta no plenário da Câmara, no entanto, integrantes da base do governo demonstraram insatisfação com a proposta encabeçada pelo ministro.

Apesar do apoio explícito do presidente Lula (PT) ao texto, o vice-líder do governo no Congresso, deputado Lindbergh Farias (PT-RJ), discursou contra o texto e se absteve da votação.

O ministro do Planejamento e Orçamento, Bruno Moretti. — Foto: Fábio Rodrigues Pozzebom/Agência Brasil

Lindbergh foi um dos integrantes do governo mais vocalmente contra o projeto. Ele é acompanhado dos deputados do Psol. Entre os argumentos, está que o Brasil não precisa de um ajuste fiscal e sim de investimentos. No entanto, o grupo é minoria entre os apoiadores do governo.

Outras quatro deputadas votaram como o parlamentar fluminense:

Outros dez parlamentares do PSOL se posicionaram em obstrução ao projeto de ajuste fiscal.

Entre os movimentos para convencer os parlamentares a aprovar a proposta, Moretti participou de uma audiência na Comissão Mista de Orçamento (CMO) .

O ministro apresentou as linhas gerais da proposta, que tem um impacto de até R$ 56 bilhões nas contas públicas em 2027.

No dia em que o texto-base foi aprovado pelo Senado, o ministro participou de conversas com parlamentares e lideranças do Congresso Nacional para explicar as medidas e buscar apoio.

Em meio à pressão do setor produtivo e de governadores, as negociações seguiram, com a atuação do ministro nos bastidores.

Em 13 de novembro, Moretti se reuniu com o presidente da Câmara, Hugo Motta (Republicanos-PB), para tratar da tramitação da proposta na Casa.

Também conversou com a bancada do PT na Câmara, em meio à resistência de parlamentares governistas a pontos do pacote .

As tratativas em torno do texto avançaram até a votação final no Senado. Moretti acompanhou a articulação no plenário, enquanto os senadores aliados do governo buscavam evitar alterações expressivas no texto.

articles.title: Records: Government, judge debated constitutional implications of searching Rep. Ilhan Omar's home
articles.summary: WASHINGTON (AP) — A magistrate judge who authorized a recent search of U. Ilhan Omar 's home by federal agents ruled that the Minnesota Democrat was entitled...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON (AP) — A magistrate judge who authorized a recent search of U.S. Rep. Ilhan Omar 's home by federal agents ruled that the Minnesota Democrat was entitled to assert her right to privacy protections afforded to sitting members of Congress at the outset of the search, according to court documents unsealed on Monday.

The unsealed filings reveal how Justice Department attorneys and U.S. Magistrate Judge Matthew Sharbaugh resolved their initial disagreement over the thorny constitutional implications of searching a member of Congress' private residence for a criminal investigation.

The heavily redacted documents — released in response to a lawsuit filed by media organizations — do not appear to shed new light on the reason or outcome of the search itself or disclose new details of an immigration-fraud investigation that Omar claims is politically motivated.

Federal authorities are investigating potential fraud in her family's immigration paperwork and have issued grand jury subpoenas to some of her relatives, The Associated Press reported last month, citing a person briefed on the investigation who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to discuss an ongoing investigation.

The unsealed filings show that Sharbaugh — before authorizing the search of Omar's home — raised concerns about the "Speech or Debate Clause" implications of searching a private residence belonging to a member of Congress. The clause, which is designed to protect legislators from executive branch interference or intimidation, includes a privilege against compelled disclosures.

Sharbaugh said he disagreed with the government's argument that the privilege is limited only to official congressional offices and certain electronic devices.

"That logic does not hold," the magistrate wrote.

Sharbaugh concluded that the government's law-enforcement interests needed to be balanced against Omar's constitutional rights as a member of Congress. He said the government ultimately agreed to a search protocol allowing Omar to invoke a privilege over any Speech or Debate Clause material before agents carried out the search.

Omar, a naturalized U.S. citizen born in Somalia, has been a target of anti-immigrant rhetoric by President Donald Trump and many Republican allies. She hasn't been charged with any crimes and has denied any wrongdoing.

Chief Judge James Boasberg ordered the partial unsealing of court filings related to the Oct. 12 search of Omar's Washington, D.C., home by Department of Homeland Security agents. He ruled after over a dozen news organizations, including The Associated Press, argued that the public has a First Amendment right to access the records.

Boasberg agreed with the government that it would be premature to unseal a 67-page search warrant affidavit containing sensitive details of the government's investigation. In a court filing last month, the government argued that it would jeopardize the investigation to unseal the court records before a charging decision is made.

An attorney for Omar didn't immediately respond to an email seeking comment Monday on the unsealed documents.

Agents conducted the court-authorized search less than a month before the Nov. 3 midterm elections, when Omar won her reelection bid. The Justice Department historically has avoided public investigative actions involving a candidate within 60 days of an election.

Omar has said DHS agents seized 17 items , including phones, notebooks, a Somali-language children's book and a vintage camera that her husband had received as a gift.

Associated Press writer Alanna Durkin Richer contributed to this report.

articles.title: What Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia teaches China's Xi about Trump
articles.summary: Huang being back at the helm of Nvidia is no guarantee of relief for Beijing.
articles.body:
Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO has riveted the world - including China, where it has become the top trending post on Weibo, the country's biggest social media platform.

Most users are pleased to see the return of the influential billionaire, who declared that he loved China, before videos appeared online of him eating noodles and drinking milk tea during a visit in May. Some wondered why - in the video of him returning to Nvidia's headquarters - he is not wearing one of his leather jackets.

But to many, Huang's return, which is being dubbed one of the greatest U-turns of all time, seems like a vindication for China.

That's probably how Xi Jinping sees it too.

Beijing has dismissed claims that one of the women who had an affair with Jensen Huang had been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security, its version of the CIA, as a spy. Chinese state media has also framed the spy saga as a smear campaign orchestrated by China hawks in Washington. The Global Times, a Communist Party mouthpiece, described it as a "witch hunt".

Now the White House, and President Donald Trump himself, have said Huang poses no national security threat, although investigations into the spy allegations are still ongoing.

Xi will have learned many lessons from this scandal, especially about Trump's pressure points.

For one, the fact that Huang's reappointment came so soon after Xi's meetings last week with Trump in Shenzhen could be read as a sign that direct engagement is an effective way to influence Washington.

Trump has said the two men discussed Huang, but did not elaborate further. Beijing has not commented.

The episode has also reinforced the view among Chinese officials that there are two camps in Washington: those in favour of restricting Chinese access to cutting edge tech to protect US national security, and those, like Huang, who believe that such restrictions will not limit Beijing's ambitions.

Huang has repeatedly argued that US export controls will force Chinese firms like Huawei to build independent alternatives - all the while shutting American companies out of the world's second-largest economy.

But him being back at the helm of Nvidia is no guarantee of relief for Beijing.

Rather, the sale of advanced chips will remain a key point of contention between the US and China, especially as the two sides try to reach a trade deal before another Trump-Xi meeting, which is expected in December.

Already new rules are being put in place that will worry Beijing.

The US Bureau of Industry and Security is tightening restrictions by targeting not only the direct export of advanced chips to China, but also Chinese firms' ability to use computing power in data centres overseas.

The measures are designed to close potential loopholes that allow Chinese companies to access advanced Nvidia and AMD chips through cloud providers operating in third countries, including Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand.

China has yet to react with measures of its own. But investors will be watching closely for any escalation which could weigh on US equity markets.

And having seen how eager Trump is to keep things stable, Xi may see this as leverage.

He now knows Trump is so worried about the stock market that he is prepared to intervene in the HR decisions of the world's biggest company. The president has also personally invested in Nvidia, although the White House has emphasised that Trump has placed his businesses in a trust managed by his sons.

China has already used its considerable chokehold over the world's rare earth metals to bring the US to the negotiating table over trade.

If Washington restricts chip exports and Beijing retaliates, that could be the start of a cycle that has a profound effect on the stock market because American companies, from car makers to defence firms to chip manufacturers, all rely on rare earths.

What China has realised is that more trouble lies ahead as it tries to build what it describes as a "constructive strategic relationship" with the US.

Trump's tariffs are no longer at the heart of that tussle. Now it's about control of critical technology and minerals which could, in turn, affect each side's military influence and economic power.

What happens next will depend on how the Jensen Huang saga unfolds because it is far from over.

Huang is set to testify before Congress next month, and come January, a Democrat-controlled Congress will raise the pressure. Even some Republican lawmakers have made clear they want answers.

Arkansas senator Tom Cotton wrote on X that the Nvidia controversy "is just the tip of the iceberg and it's not resolved because Jensen Huang has his job back".

articles.title: Trump says Jensen Huang's Nvidia return is not a national security risk. Why are others concerned?
articles.summary: Huang reportedly had an affair with a Chinese spy at the same time Nvidia was selling her company advanced chips.
articles.body:
When news broke Monday that Nvidia had reinstated Jensen Huang as its president and CEO less than two weeks after he resigned amid reports of multiple extramarital affairs — including one with a woman suspected of spying for China — President Trump was quick to reassure the public that "the United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security."

"People say, 'Is it a threat to have him?' No, it's a threat to lose him," Trump told CNBC shortly after the announcement .

But not everyone agrees . Before Huang resigned, the Trump administration's own intelligence officials reportedly identified Alice Huang — the Chinese-born leader of a Southeast Asian company called Megaspeed — as a Chinese intelligence asset who kept in touch with Beijing's top spy agency for more than a year while she targeted the Nvidia chief.

Why does this matter? Without government authorization, U.S. export controls prohibit Nvidia from selling certain advanced AI microchips — the chips that have powered the artificial intelligence boom — directly to China, America's main AI competitor. But during a period when Jensen and Alice Huang were seen dining and socializing together , Megaspeed wound up buying billions of dollars' worth of those same Nvidia chips.

And Megaspeed not only has ties to Beijing . It's actually under federal investigation for potentially smuggling advanced Nvidia semiconductors out of the U.S. and into China.

On Monday, the commerce department added Megaspeed to a trade blacklist , saying it had been "determined by the U.S. Government to be acting contrary to the national security or foreign policy interests of the United States."

As a result, Huang's reinstatement triggered immediate bipartisan backlash. Outgoing Republican Rep. Don Bacon of Nebraska accused Huang of being "compromised and exploited by a Chinese spy" and said "Nvidia should have moved on" without him.

"Congress needs to get to the bottom of who approved high end computer chips sales to China," Bacon wrote on social media . "We cannot say we want to win the AI race and then give China our best technology. We need sunlight on who is responsible."

Sen. John Cornyn — another retiring Republican lawmaker — questioned Trump's seemingly cavalier attitude toward Huang and China.

"No national security risk?" Cornyn posted . "Based on what?"

Democrat Sen. Elizabeth Warren, who is set to take over the Senate banking committee in January, posted on X, "This reckless decision to bring back Jensen Huang does not change the fact that Huang and NVIDIA still owe Congress answers." She said Trump needs to explain what "input" was given and by which senior officials to support Huang's reinstatement.

On Monday, Trump took credit for Huang's return, saying he had spoken directly to Nvidia's board. "I convinced them," the president told CNBC . "I made the deal."

The U.S. position on chip sales to China has seesawed over the last 18 months. In April 2025, the Trump administration imposed its first major restrictions on AI semiconductor sales outside the U.S., toughening rules created by the Biden administration. But after several meetings between Trump and Huang — who consistently lobbied for letting chip companies do business with China — the administration eventually approved sales of Nvidia's second-most-powerful chip to Beijing.

At the same time, " advisers to Trump told him on at least two occasions that U.S. intelligence had uncovered Ms. Huang's links to the Chinese spy agency and that she was in a close relationship with Mr. Huang while he was still running Nvidia," according to the New York Times .

But Trump "downplayed the concerns" and refused to intervene because he "regarded Mr. Huang as a valuable ally and Nvidia as essential to the health of the American economy and stock market," U.S. officials with direct knowledge of the briefings told the paper. Meanwhile

After Jensen stepped down, Trump went on to muse about his return and question whether Alice Huang was a Chinese intelligence asset, denying that anyone in his government had ever told him that.

"I don't know that she is a spy," the president told reporters last week . "Usually, what happens with that is that any woman coming to the country that's a beautiful woman that comes from China, they say she's a spy."

On Sunday, Trump called for Huang's return on social media. The New York Times reported that it came after "several days of maneuvering to provide the company's board with assurances that Mr. Huang was not facing criminal charges and did not pose a national security risk." That maneuvering reportedly included directing Vice President JD Vance, who has close ties to Silicon Valley, to speak with both Huang and Nvidia's board.

On Monday, the board announced that it had voted unanimously to reinstate Huang. Trump responded by calling Huang "a Great Patriot and National Treasure" and insisting that "the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct."

In the same post, Trump added that "NVIDIA should continue its thorough internal investigation of the Company's compliance with U.S. export controls in order to ensure that it is fulfilling its legal obligations and Patriotic Duty to protect U.S. National Security."

But an internal probe is unlikely to satisfy Congress. Huang is already set to deliver closed-door testimony on Dec. 1 before three congressional committees led by Republicans — and Democrats have signaled that they will keep investigating the issue when they take control of the House and Senate next year.

On Monday, Democratic Sen. Ruben Gallego of Arizona accused Trump of "selling out our national security to keep the stock market high." Another Democrat, Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker, said on social media that "this is the greed and lack of accountability that the country just rejected."

"There are serious national security concerns being raised about Jensen Huang that should not be papered over by this administration or the Nvidia board," Pritzker added.

The president is a significant investor in Nvidia stock. Last week, the Washington Post reported that by August 2026, Trump held a $13 million to $62 million stake in Nvidia — up from as little as $615,000 at the end of 2024.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had also accused the commerce department, led by Howard Lutnick, of stalling efforts by the treasury, defense and state departments, as well as the U.S. trade representative, to block chip sales to Megaspeed.

"Commerce has the pen," Bessent said on CNBC earlier this month . "You will have to ask them about their internal processes."

Lutnick's former firm Cantor Fitzgerald — now led by his sons — has business relationships with Southeast Asian data centers, leading lawmakers on both sides of the aisle to question "whether Lutnick compromised national security to make money for his family," according to the Guardian .

Lutnick should have taken "the threats of communist China more seriously," Republican Sen. Tom Cotton of Arkansas told the Wall Street Journal last week . Congressional Democrats have said they plan to investigate Lutnick in 2027.

articles.title: La réplica de Bono a Felipe González: "Quiero que el Gobierno de España sea progresista. Prefiero ser pro Bono que pro PP"
articles.standfirst: El exdirigente socialista advierte del arrepentimiento en otros países y busca movilizar votantes
articles.summary: El exdirigente socialista advierte del arrepentimiento en otros países y busca movilizar votantes
articles.body: José Bono ha salido al paso de la postura de Felipe González marcando distancias respecto a cualquier confrontación personal o partidista, al tiempo que ha fijado su prioridad política en la continuidad de un Ejecutivo de izquierdas. El exministro y expresidente de Castilla-La Mancha ha dejado claro que su motivación no responde a intereses particulares ni a una disputa con el expresidente del Gobierno. En este sentido, ha resumido su posición afirmando: "No quiero nada. Lo único que quiero es que el Gobierno de España sea un gobierno progresista y que no tengamos que lamentar lo que en otros países lamentan y con qué nivel de arrepentimiento. Estoy pensando quienes votaron a Milei y les apareció con la motosierra. Quienes votaron a Trump y, y se encontraron, bueno, con lo que se han encontrado." Para Bono, la referencia a la situación política en otros escenarios internacionales sirve como advertencia sobre las consecuencias que pueden derivarse de determinadas decisiones electorales. Frente a ese panorama, el exdirigente socialista ha defendido que la apuesta por un proyecto progresista es el eje central de su intervención pública. Al abordar directamente el debate generado en torno a Felipe González, Bono ha optado por zanjar la cuestión sin alimentar polémicas internas y subrayando que no desea entrar en un choque con él. Según ha expresado literalmente: "Yo prefiero que sea pro Bono que pro PP. El tema de Felipe González, vamos, como decimos en mi tierra, chimpún. Yo lo último que quiero es pelear con Felipe González. Pues si ya ha votado, como dicen en Roma, Roma locuta, causa finita." Lejos de detenerse en el posicionamiento de un solo votante, Bono ha trasladado el foco hacia una movilización más amplia entre la ciudadanía que comparte ese nombre o representa a un electorado más extenso. Con ese argumento, ha señalado: "Yo voy a pelearme por el voto de otros muchos Felipes, que no es el único Felipe que hay en España." Por último, Bono ha interpretado que la controversia suscitada puede tener un efecto contrario al que cabría esperar y traducirse en un respaldo electoral hacia el actual presidente del Gobierno. Así lo ha planteado al cerrar su reflexión: "Este debate que ha ocurrido, ¿sabes para lo que ha valido? A lo mejor no para que venga un voto, sino para que vengan unos cuantos cientos de miles de votos que dicen: 'Pedro Sánchez no se merece esto'."

articles.title: Rufián y Figo reavivan su enfrentamiento en las redes sociales: "Suelta ya mi brazo, pesetas"
articles.standfirst: Este intercambio es otro en una serie de reproches que han ocurrido en los últimos días en X
articles.summary: Este intercambio es otro en una serie de reproches que han ocurrido en los últimos días en X
articles.body: La campaña electoral para las elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre ha traído un nuevo capítulo de tensión a X. Gabriel Rufián y Luís Figo se han vuelto a reprochar después de que el portavoz de Esquerra Republicana publicara un mensaje con una palabra: "Pásalo". La publicación reavivó la disputa que ambos han estado teniendo durante varios días con las redes sociales como escenario. El exfutbolista portugués citó el mensaje del diputado. En su comentario criticó a Rufián por estar en política y recibir una remuneración por ello: "140 mil pavos" escribió Figo refiriéndose al salario del republicano antes de añadir que ni siquiera "tus primos" votarían por él. El intercambio pasó entonces de la ironía política a los reproches personales. Rufián no tardó en responder. El líder de ERC publicó el post del exjugador y utilizó una frase para responder al enfrentamiento: "Suelta ya mi brazo, pesetas". La frase también hacía referencia a uno de los episodios más famosos de Figo: su salida del FC Barcelona al Real Madrid en el año 2000. Pero esto no se quedó aquí ya que Luís Figo no se quedaría callado. De hecho, la leyenda del Real Madrid ponía en su cuenta una imagen del momento donde Rufián le dijo a Óscar Puente aquello de "has sido un gran ministro" rodeado de un accidente de tren emulando a lo sucedido en Adamuz y Urda. Todo ello con un mensaje: "Agárrale bien predicador". Palabras a las que Gabriel Rufián contestó con la imagen de la cabeza de cochinillo que le lanzaron en su época de futbolista y cambió el FC Barcelona por el Real Madrid. El enfrentamiento no surge de forma aislada. La relación entre ambos se ha vuelto tensa durante la campaña después de que Rufián se refiriera al exfutbolista en un evento celebrado en Tarragona. En ese mitin, el diputado bromeó sobre Figo siendo "Ministro de Deportes" en un hipotético gobierno del PP y Vox. Esa mención abrió una nueva línea de confrontación entre dos figuras de campos muy diferentes. Desde entonces los mensajes han estado volando de un lado a otro en X. Figo ha acusado al político catalán de "vivir del cuento" mientras que Rufián ha respondido recordando episodios del pasado del portugués: entre otros ha recordado los titulares deportivos publicados antes de su fichaje por el Real Madrid cuando el jugador aún negaba que iba a dejar el Barcelona. La controversia ha convertido lo que comenzó como un intercambio de publicaciones en uno de los enfrentamientos más discutidos de la campaña en las redes sociales. Ninguna de las partes ha bajado el tono hasta ahora y cada nueva intervención alimenta una disputa que mezcla política, fútbol y memoria deportiva.

articles.body:
Officials from the U.S. Army and Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) will brief reporters Tuesday morning on the planned detonation of lead-containing munitions in Iowa.

The operation, slated for Wednesday after a previous delay , has sparked widespread concern over the potential health and environmental impacts of lead exposure.

President Trump injected further uncertainty into the plans Monday, as he sought approval for the detonation from Iowa Gov.-elect Rob Sand (D), who maintained the decision rests with the administration. That decision came after a federal court declined to intervene .

Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle later confirmed the operation would proceed.

The press conference will feature Telle, FEMA Administrator Cameron Hamilton and other federal officials.

The event is scheduled to begin at 10 a.m. EST.

articles.title: Cotton warns White House over push to keep hemp products on store shelves
articles.summary: Sen. Tom Cotton (R-Ark.), the No. 3 member of Senate GOP leadership, is warning the White House to drop its request to add language to a year-end funding deal that Cotton says would keep intoxicating hemp-derived products on gas station shelves in 2027. “The administration’s year-end funding request proposes to keep gas-station candy marijuana on…
articles.body:
Sen. Tom Cotton (R-Ark.), the No. 3 member of Senate GOP leadership, is warning the White House to drop its request to add language to a year-end funding deal that Cotton says would keep intoxicating hemp-derived products on gas station shelves in 2027.

“The administration’s year-end funding request proposes to keep gas-station candy marijuana on the shelves. The request includes many urgent needs, especially for national security and funding our troops, but gas-station weed isn’t one of them,” Cotton posted on the social platform X.

He noted Congress voted to ban “these dangerous products” in 2025 and warned if the White House insists on adding language to a government funding deal to further delay the ban, it would “threaten the entire bill.”

BestReviews is reader-supported and may earn an affiliate commission.

Congress included language in the federal funding measure that ended the 43-day government shutdown in 2025 to ban the sale of most intoxicating hemp-derived products, such as delta-8 and delta-9.

The ban was due to take effect on Nov. 12 of this year, but the Senate voted in August to delay its implementation until Dec. 11, matching it with the expiration of government funding.

The White House on Monday proposed adding language to any stopgap government funding resolution to “allow Americans to benefit from access to nonintoxicating full-spectrum CBD products” while restricting products “that pose serious health risks.”

But Cotton on Monday called out the language submitted by the White House in its request of “anomalies” to be added to the government funding bill as another attempt to circumvent a ban on intoxicating hemp-derived products.

“Congress banned these dangerous products last year. If the administration pushes for yet another delay of the ban—which it promised not to do in August—this misplaced priority will threaten the entire bill,” Cotton wrote.

More than a dozen Republican senators, led by Sen. Ted Budd (R-N.C.), sent a letter to Trump on Friday asking him not to delay the Dec. 11 deadline for banning intoxicating hemp products.

“The choice is simple: stand with American families who don’t want candy-flavored drugs sold in gas stations or with the cartel who profits from addiction and devastation,” the senators wrote. “There can be no last-minute ‘framework’ that keeps these drugs on store shelves.”

They pointed out that the Senate voted 76-24 last year to end the sale of intoxicating THC products.

“In September, you signed a one-month extension, moving the effective date to Dec. 11, 2026. Your administration made clear at the time that there would be no further extensions. We ask that you hold to that commitment. Every extension is only a victory for the companies selling those products but a loss for the families who are paying the price,” they wrote.

articles.title: Controlled Iowa munitions detonation better than ‘worst-case scenario,’ acting Army secretary says
articles.summary: Federal officials said scheduling the mitigated blast for Wednesday morning — the day before Thanksgiving and ahead of evening snow — prevents cold temperatures from creating more unstable crystals.
articles.body: A controlled detonation is the safest way to dispose of the unstable lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant and avoids the "worst-case scenario" of a spontaneous blast, Acting U.S. Army Secretary Adam Telle said Tuesday. The Army will detonate the bomb-making materials on Wednesday at 9 a.m. local time — the day before Thanksgiving — after a federal appeals court rejected a legal challenge and allowed the mitigation effort to go forward. "We have talked to every expert within the federal government and every expert we could find outside the federal government," Telle told reporters during a news conference. "A controlled, mitigated detonation of the lead azide here at Iowa Army Ammunition Plant is far preferable to an uncontrolled spontaneous detonation of that substance." Federal officials said they are minimizing the impact of the controlled detonation at the plant in Middletown, Iowa, by using two-story-high sand-filled barriers, water walls made of eight 16,000-gallon tanks and gel blocks to absorb the blast. The Army has also deployed misters and specialized PFAS-free foams to trap lead dust from the 68 barrels of lead azide, which hold more than 9,700 pounds net explosive weight. FEDERAL APPEALS COURT CLEARS ARMY TO DETONATE VOLATILE IOWA EXPLOSIVES AS DEM GOV-ELECT REFUSES TO SIGN OFF According to Ford County, Illinois, one of the neighboring states, lead azide is "a highly sensitive explosive compound commonly used as an initiating explosive in detonators and blasting caps. It is one of the primary materials used to start the detonation sequence in military, mining, demolition, and commercial explosive applications." Officials said they ruled out chemical neutralization because the drums deteriorated rapidly over the past eight months, leaving crystallized lead azide on the outside of the barrels and lids that makes moving or opening them too dangerous. In a release on Tuesday, the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) said it has mobilized more than 100 personnel and contractors alongside the Army, FEMA, the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and other federal partners to protect communities in Iowa, Missouri and Illinois. EPA Associate Administrator for National Security and Operations Coordination Tom Croci said the agency has deployed three mobile labs and an air toxics lab and is "putting the full force of the agency behind this effort to ensure we are doing everything possible to protect human health and the environment." The agency said it has collected over 1,001 pre-detonation air, land and water samples in the communities surrounding Middletown and will continue sampling during and after the blast in coordination with the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) to guide any necessary lead remediation. IOWA RESIDENTS NEAR AMMUNITION PLANT TOLD TO VACATE BEFORE ARMY DETONATES 5 TONS OF BOMB-MAKING CHEMICALS Even with those safeguards, current weather models show the plume — which will contain some level of lead particles — may affect about 350 farms, according to Department of Agriculture Undersecretary Richard Fordyce. Local and federal officials are strongly urging all residents inside the evacuation zone — defined by the Army as a 5-mile cone extending southwest of the plant — to leave ahead of the blast. Sean Kaufman, an official with the Department of Health and Human Services, placed particular emphasis on vulnerable residents, saying pregnant women, children and people with chronic illnesses should evacuate the area projected to be affected by the detonation. Those outside the area should "do what you need to do to take care of your family," Kaufman said, adding that it is crucial to stay indoors during the scheduled blast. IOWA'S GOVERNOR-ELECT HAS A MESSAGE FOR DEMOCRATS GEARING UP TO FIGHT TRUMP In a statement Tuesday afternoon, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) provided a list of recommendations for those who live close to the munitions plant, including closing all windows and doors, sealing any gaps to prevent outside air from coming in and setting up furnaces to recirculate air with filters rated MERV 11 or higher. The CDC also said that lead dust can get on clothes and shoes, and be transferred into your home that way. "Wash or remove your shoes before entering a building if you think they may have been exposed to lead. Wash clothes and hands before touching your face or eating," the CDC said. Telle said federal agencies will continue updating the public over the next 24 hours, as shifting weather forecasts could alter the path of any dust kicked up by the blast. The Army has also held town halls in communities where the effects will be the most acute, Telle said. Beginning six hours before the detonation, the Army will disseminate updated impact maps on an hourly basis that will take into account the most recent weather forecasts. Telle and other officials said they scheduled the detonation for Wednesday morning to take advantage of favorable weather patterns before snow is forecast to arrive later that evening. Cold temperatures and temperature fluctuations could cause the lead azide to form additional unstable crystals that can self-detonate from heat, shock or friction. Munitions specialists had warned about this in court filings. The controlled detonation has already been postponed three times amid public concern over toxic lead dust. In a public advisory, the Army said Wednesday's blast will produce two rapid detonations, ground vibrations and a dust plume expected to linger for no more than an hour. For anyone living southwest of the plant who wants to leave, FEMA will provide temporary lodging until Nov. 27 with extensions available upon request. Food, water, emergency transportation and other supplies will also be handed out to relocated populations. Residents can register at DisasterAssistance.gov or call 1-800-621-3362. In Iowa, Republican Gov. Kim Reynolds issued a disaster emergency proclamation on Tuesday for Des Moines, Lee and Van Buren counties, unlocking state response resources and approving up to 100 federally activated Iowa National Guard soldiers to assist about 150 households with evacuation outreach. "Today’s briefing by the U.S. Army highlighted the responsible planning and coordination that have gone into the upcoming detonation. I greatly appreciate their due diligence, responsible approach, and focus on the public health and safety of Iowans in nearby communities," Reynolds said in a statement. State officials also advised residents between five and 20 miles southwest of the plant to shelter indoors with windows closed and issued updated guidance for livestock producers within 20 miles. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP To prevent similar incidents at other military installations storing dangerous chemicals, Telle said he ordered the Army on Tuesday to "begin a thorough examination of every such weapons storage facility within the Army's inventory." After the detonation is completed, the CDC said it would "support Iowa with any post-event community health assessment needs." Federal officials said that if any residential property tests above the EPA-approved standard of 200 parts per million, remediation teams will remove affected soil and clean surfaces at full government expense, and the U.S. Army Claims Service will immediately process claims for any vibration damage.

articles.title: Democrats: Don’t fear the veto
articles.summary: If Democrats want to hamper the public’s approval of President Trump and his party, they should pursue energetic initiatives despite his veto threats.
articles.body:
Since Democrats’ decisive victory in the midterm election, President Trump has added a new decoration to the Oval Office: a red hat emblazoned with the word “VETO.” Although Democrats will control Congress come January 2027, Trump’s threat to become “Mr. Veto” and “veto everything” has sparked lively internal debate concerning how they should legislate in anticipation of presidential opposition.

Some, like Sen. Brian Schatz (D-Hawaii), argue that the party should not make proposals that Trump “is guaranteed to veto” because that would be “wasted energy.” Others, like Rep. Greg Casar (D-Texas), assert Democrats should pursue ambitious legislation and make the president use his veto on their “popular, pro-affordability policies.”

Recent political science scholarship on presidential vetoes suggests Democrats like Casar have a point. While Trump may veto legislation they pass, forcing the president to use his veto can be politically beneficial because it erodes public support for him and his party, which could position Democrats for further victories in 2028. However, in pursuing this strategy, Democrats should focus on policies with broad popular support and not make their provocations too obvious.

Central to Americans’ notion of democracy is that majorities rule , and when Congress passes legislation, it does so with the support of majorities of the people’s representatives. Given Democrats’ historic margins of victory , the size of the coalitions passing legislation for the next two years will far exceed the bare majorities required. This imprimatur of majority support poses a challenge for presidents like Trump who want to block legislation. By exercising their veto, they risk appearing to obstruct the popular will.

This obstruction can damage presidents’ public standing for two reasons. First, the choice to unilaterally block policies can trigger Americans’ skepticism of excessive executive power. Indeed, recent studies show only roughly half of Americans support the president’s ability to veto legislation. Further, people are more likely to oppose a president’s veto when they disapprove of him. Since Trump’s approval rating is at a historically low level , many people would likely react negatively should he use his veto pen.

Second, when a president vetoes legislation, the public often perceives him to hold extreme preferences out of step with its policy priorities. Consequently, presidents who issue vetoes often see their job approval decline. For instance, Tim Groseclose and Nolan McCarty have shown that presidents’ approval ratings fall by about 2 percentage points each time they veto major legislation during divided government.

These findings suggest that if Democrats want to hamper the public’s approval of Trump and his party, they should pursue energetic initiatives despite his veto threats. However, this strategy’s success depends on which policies Democrats pursue and how well they frame their efforts as sincere attempts to legislate.

First, in order to frame the president’s veto as out of touch with public opinion, Democrats must ensure the underlying policy is popular. As Andrew Reeves and his coauthors show , when a president vetoes an unpopular bill, his approval rating can stay steady or even increase. In this scenario, the president can cast his veto as protecting the public from a disfavored policy and perhaps erode Congress’ public support.

Therefore, Democrats would benefit more from eliciting a veto on a popular initiative like restoring Affordable Care Act subsidies rather than on something more controversial, such as increasing taxes on the wealthy .

Second, if the public thinks Congress knew the president would veto the legislation, they may punish Congress for prioritizing political gamesmanship over advancing practical policies that would improve their lives. Ryan Williamson and Joel Sievert demonstrate people are more likely to blame Congress than the president when a veto occurs if told Congress knew the president would exercise his veto. As Democrats pursue legislation likely to draw Trump’s veto, they must frame their actions as good faith policymaking rather than cynical provocations.

Democrats, don’t fear the veto. As long as you pass legislation the public supports and do so as a serious exercise in governance, Trump’s vetoes are likely to depress public support for him and the Republican Party while helping you promote your agenda for 2028.

And, hey, if Trump decides the political costs of vetoes are too high and your proposals become law, you’ll get some policy wins earlier than expected.

David Miller is an assistant professor in American University’s Department of Government.

Fox News host Jesse Watters said Monday that President Trump’s defense of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang will give Democrats “ammunition” to go after the president — and potentially pursue impeachment.

“The Democrats are now licking their chops over the Jensen affair and Trump personally restoring him as CEO, even if it was to help the economy and the country,” Watters said. “This gives them a lot of ammunition. The Democrats will likely use this scandal to impeach.”

Huang was restored as CEO on Monday despite revelations of extramarital affairs — including one with a woman the U.S. government suspected of being a Chinese spy — after Trump’s public and private defense of the tech executive. Trump said he personally urged the board to restore Huang to lead the company he co-founded, and a source confirmed to The Hill that Vice President Vance also played a role in the push.

Huang’s return to Nvidia drew bipartisan scrutiny and is likely to be the subject of congressional investigations. The CEO is already set to testify before the Senate Banking Committee, and Republicans are even calling for Congress to investigate Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, the suspected spy.

With Democrats set to reclaim majorities in both chambers next year, investigations are even more likely to take place.

Democrats are “going to say Trump put our national security at risk and is bowing to the Chinese, and a bunch of Republicans in Congress aren’t going to defend him, so this is going to get ugly — fast,” the “Primetime” host said.

“And a billionaire, foreign-born chip king, a Republican donor, who cheats on his wife and is tech war profiteering, isn’t the most sympathetic character for the president’s party to defend,” he added.

Top Democrats have not said they plan to impeach Trump, but they have not ruled it out either. In a recent interview with The New York Times, House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.) said he has faith in Democrats to properly seek accountability.

“I have great trust in the legislative leaders of this effort and every single Democrat who’s on the Oversight Committee. We’ve done accountability in this Congress,” Jeffries told the Times.

Democrats impeached Trump twice in his first term, and he was acquitted on both occasions. Several Democrats have expressed concern that moving to impeach him a third time could backfire, and it would be unlikely to yield a conviction even with Democrats’ expanded Senate majority.

articles.title: Lessons from air traffic control chaos for Medicare for All
articles.summary: In an opinion piece, Merrill Matthews argues that the recent air traffic control crisis provides several warnings against the Democratic push for “Medicare for All,” suggesting that a government-run healthcare system would lead to technological delays, funding shortages and staffing issues.
articles.body:
There are lots of lessons to be learned from the recent air traffic control chaos — and not just about air traffic control. Many of those lessons apply to the current Democratic push for Medicare for All . What are some of those lessons?

First, the air traffic control system is a government-run program. Medicare for All would also be government run. Medicare for All is not an expansion of the current Medicare program that covers most seniors, as the name of the proposal deceptively implies. Medicare for All eliminates Medicare, as well as the Medicaid program and all private health insurance, including the 165 million Americans who have employer-provided health insurance.

Under Medicare for All the government — the same politicians and bureaucrats who oversee air traffic control — will run health care. They will determine what drugs, medical devices and services patients can have and when they can have them — if they can have them at all.

Second, the government delayed access to the newest air-traffic control technology, which we now learn is grossly outdated.

Experts claimed that part of the system goes back to the 1990s and still runs on copper wire instead of fiber. The shutdown that stranded thousands of planes and millions of passengers was due a glitch while belatedly patching the outdated system.

Government-run health care systems also delay access to the newest technology. Take Great Britain’s National Health Service, one of the models for U.S. reform. The Guardian has written , “Patients could face delays accessing drugs on the NHS after health bosses agreed that the most expensive treatments can be stalled.”

Or how about this from Canada , another model for U.S. reform. “Out of G7 nations, Canadian patients on public plans have the longest average wait time for new drugs.”

U.S. patients currently have access to the latest technology, whether it’s diagnostic tests, medical devices, innovative surgeries or prescription drugs. That will come to an end under Medicare for All, just as it has in other government-run health care systems.

When Medicare for All proponents claim patients will have access to all the latest medical technology and services, don’t believe them. It didn’t happen with air traffic control, even though on any day millions of lives are at stake, and it won’t happen in health care, even though on any day millions of lives are also at stake.

The third lesson is there is never enough federal money. You will hear Medicare for All advocates assure voters the system will be fully funded. But that didn’t happen in the air traffic control, and it won’t happen in health care.

Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy is using the current crisis to ask for $20 billion, which he upped to $50 billion . Incoming Democrats may or may not approve the funding. And that’s because all federal spending, including health care, becomes a political battle.

A fourth lesson is that limited funding leads to staffing shortages. According to the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis , there were 44,000 air traffic controllers in 2012. That number dropped to 35,000 in 2018 and 30,000 in 2025 — even though there were many more planes in the air. Even so, the controllers do a great job with the tools they have.

There will also be far fewer doctors and other medical professionals under Medicare for All.

The Canadian Medical Association recognizes many Canadians go to the U.S. to get needed health care in a timely manner, “Given Canada’s health care system’s struggles with doctor shortages and long waits for procedures, it’s believable.” And a new report from the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation says “4.5 million Canadians who are middle aged and older have had trouble accessing specialist care.”

A final lesson is that no one wants to take responsibility for government failures. President Trump blamed traffic control problems on the Biden administration. But the negligence goes back decades, under both Republicans and Democrats. As for Congress, it’s claiming most of the $12.5 billion appropriated for air traffic control reform hasn’t been used — so don’t blame them.

Under Medicare for All, the government will say it has provided adequate funding. Hospitals, doctors and other medical providers will complain they are being overworked and underpaid. Medical device and drug companies may cut back on their research and development because the funds under a government-controlled system will be limited. And patients will see waiting lines grow and access to innovative therapies decline.

Ironically, many air-traffic-control experts want to turn the government-run system over to the private sector while Democrats say we need to turn the privately run heath system over to the government.

Yes, we have many problems in the U.S. health care system. But this comes 16 years after Democrats passed an ObamaCare system with no Republican support, which is clearly broken. Now, Democrats say Medicare for All will fix a broken system they claimed to have fixed 16 years ago. They were wrong then, and they’re wrong now.

Merrill Matthews is the Texas state chair of Our Republican Legacy.

articles.title: Giuliani ‘very, very humbled’ to be getting Presidential Medal of Freedom
articles.summary: President Trump will award former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani (R) the Presidential Medal of Freedom on Tuesday, more than a year after he announced plans to bestow the nation’s highest civilian honor on his longtime ally. Giuliani, 82, revealed during a Monday appearance on Steve Bannon’s “War Room” podcast that Trump would present…
articles.body:
President Trump will award former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani (R) the Presidential Medal of Freedom on Tuesday, more than a year after he announced plans to bestow the nation’s highest civilian honor on his longtime ally.

Giuliani, 82, revealed during a Monday appearance on Steve Bannon’s “War Room” podcast that Trump would present him with the medal during an 11 a.m. EST ceremony in the Oval Office.

“I’m of course very, very humbled and very honored not only to receive it but to receive it from him,” Giuliani said.

White House spokesperson Olivia Wales confirmed the ceremony to NewsNation, praising Giuliani’s record as a federal prosecutor and his leadership of New York City in the aftermath of the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks.

“Mayor Rudy Giuliani is a dedicated public servant whose decisive leadership has left a lasting impact on New York City and our Nation. As U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of New York, Mayor Giuliani took down mob bosses and led a relentless war on crime. As Mayor, he transformed New York from a crime-ridden city into one of the safest big cities in the world, fostering economic opportunity and cultural greatness,” Wales said in a statement.

She continued, “President Trump will proudly honor Mayor Giuliani – America’s Mayor – with the Presidential Medal of Freedom for his lifetime of service to the American people.”

Trump first announced his intention to honor Giuliani in September 2025, two days after the former mayor was seriously injured in a car crash in New Hampshire. At the time, the president called Giuliani the “greatest Mayor in the history of New York City, and an equally great American Patriot.”

Giuliani, who served as mayor from 1994 to 2001 and unsuccessfully sought the Republican presidential nomination in 2008, was one of Trump’s most vocal defenders and faced legal troubles over his role in the efforts to overturn the results of the 2020 presidential election.

The former U.S. associate attorney general and U.S. attorney for the Southern District of New York was permanently disbarred from practicing law in New York and Washington, D.C., after promoting false claims of election fraud. He also faced criminal charges in Georgia and Arizona stemming from efforts to reverse Trump’s electoral defeat. Giuliani has denied wrongdoing.

In 2023, he was ordered by a federal jury to pay $148 million in damages to two former Georgia election workers whom he falsely accused of election fraud and reached a settlement .
